definitions.explanation: An honorific suffix used for boys, younger men, or male subordinates.
Sometimes used for female colleagues or subordinates.

examples.japanese: {太郎|たろう}{君|くん}、⟦{遊|あそ}ぼう→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
{田中|たなか}{君|くん}、⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧⟦{来|き}て→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: Tanaka, come here for a moment.

examples.japanese: {山田|やまだ}{君|くん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦とき→時：02918_toki⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Yamada has been my friend since elementary school.

examples.japanese: {佐藤|さとう}{君|くん}、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{資料|しりょう}→資料：04166_shiryou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦コピーして→コピーする：02941_kopiisuru⟧⟦くれ→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。

⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{女性|じょせい}→女性：01617_josei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{社員|しゃいん}→社員：03065_shain⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{君|くん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧。
examples.english: The department manager also addresses female employees with -kun.

examples.japanese: ⟦うち→内：01328_uchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{男女|だんじょ}→男女：03117_danjo⟧⟦{問|と}わず→問う：02299_tou⟧⟦{若|わか}い→若い：00823_wakai⟧⟦{社員|しゃいん}→社員：03065_shain⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{君|くん}づけ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: At our company, many supervisors address young employees with -kun regardless of gender.

notes:
〜{君|くん} is an honorific suffix primarily used for males, indicating familiarity and mild respect.

WHO USES IT:
- Teachers addressing male students
- Superiors addressing younger or junior colleagues (sometimes female too)
- Among male friends of similar age
- Parents to sons or boys

COMPARISON OF SUFFIXES:
- 〜⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧: polite, gender-neutral (the safe default)
- 〜{君|くん}: familiar, mainly for males
- 〜⟦ちゃん→ちゃん：02003_chan⟧: affectionate, mainly for females/children
- 〜⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧: very formal and respectful

WORKPLACE NOTE:
In some companies, {君|くん} is used for both male and female employees by superiors. This practice varies; some consider it outdated for addressing women. Using ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧ is always safe.

WATCH OUT:
Do not use {君|くん} for superiors or older people — it can sound condescending.
